clue.text: In direct confrontation — unlike Charles I in 1650

definitions.meaning: meeting face to face, front to front, with nothing in between
King Charles I was beheaded in January 1649, so by 1650 he no longer had his head attached

explanation.surface: A history quiz contrasting a bold confrontation with the fate of a beheaded king.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means meeting something frontally; read literally it describes a body still topped by a skull, which the executed king lacked.

clue.text: Strange things showing up in company tax that's fiddled

indicators.note: accounts that are fiddled are cooked, so these letters are juggled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
i.e. (id est) is Latin shorthand for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Odd items turn up in a company's tax return that has been cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddled' rearranges COTAXIE (CO, TAX and IE) into the answer; 'showing up in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotic items are foreign and unusual curiosities, so the plural noun covers strange things.

clue.text: Erase "p" in "empty"

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the word for erase, as the clue literally instructs

parts.note: to erase is to delete
the letter itself, taken as written

explanation.surface: An editing instruction: strike out the letter p inside the word 'empty'.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a proofreader's order to remove a letter; actually DELETE (erase) has P put in it, and 'empty' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete a store is to drain or exhaust it, a verb synonym of empty.

clue.text: Garment that could be almost covering sleeper in US

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sits above the other, so it covers it

parts.note: nigh means nearly or almost
a railway sleeper is called a tie in American usage

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing that might nearly cover a sleeping American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' works only because this is a down light, one piece sitting above the other. 'sleeper' suggests a person in bed, but here it is the railway beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, a loose item of women's clothing worn in bed.

clue.text: Lofty sort of view one may take of plant

definitions.text: Lofty sort of view one may take
definitions.meaning: a view seen from high above, as a flying creature would see the ground
the name of various small flowers such as a primrose and a speedwell

explanation.surface: Someone surveys a factory from a great height.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory to be viewed, but it is a second definition: a flower name.
explanation.definitionFit: An overhead panorama is described with this term, which also names a primula and a speedwell species.

clue.text: Travellers on the road may be experiencing problems

definitions.text: Travellers on the road may be
definitions.meaning: people journeying by road might ride in a horse-drawn wagon
a British informal phrase for being in trouble or a fix

explanation.surface: Motorists on a journey might run into difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom means in trouble; literally it is riding in a wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: The British colloquial idiom means in a difficult or awkward situation, so it suits being in trouble.

clue.text: Hurry up rate of progress — it's a long way away!

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to hurry is to speed
pace is the rate at which something moves forward

explanation.surface: A call to quicken progress because the destination is very distant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' signals a turn only because the light runs downward; the exclamation makes the definition sound like a remark rather than a phrase for remote outer regions.
explanation.definitionFit: The region of the universe far beyond the Earth's atmosphere is remote by any measure.

clue.text: Ambiguous quote about American spirit taken the wrong way

indicators.note: being taken in the wrong direction means the whole assembled string is read backwards
the word for quote goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to quote is to cite
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: An unclear remark about American liquor gets misinterpreted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts AMGIN inside CITE, giving CITAMGINE; 'taken the wrong way' turns the whole thing back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mysterious or puzzling is open to more than one reading, hence unclear.

clue.text: Tree-bark displayed in office of church

parts.note: an elder is a tree
a bark (barque) is a sailing ship

explanation.surface: Bark from a tree is put on show in a church office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tree-bark' reads as one thing, the outer layer of a trunk, but splits into two pieces, and 'bark' is a vessel, not tree skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Elders hold a position of authority in Presbyterian and other churches, and the suffix makes it the post itself.

clue.text: Drama featuring son and grandfather, perhaps

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
OAP is old-age pensioner, as a grandfather might well be

explanation.surface: A TV serial whose cast includes a boy and his grandpa.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP (old-age pensioner) is the British term for a retired person drawing a state pension.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for soap opera, a long-running serial drama on TV or radio.

clue.text: At Christmas, most of us will be shown disapproval

definitions.text: At Christmas, most of us will
definitions.meaning: most families acquire a turkey for the festive dinner
an idiom for being booed or hissed off, as a poor performer is

explanation.surface: A gloomy prediction that the festive season will bring general scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird is the Christmas turkey; the idiom comes from theatre hissing, which sounds like geese.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be jeered or rejected by an audience, as a failing act is.

clue.text: Bison appearing in erudite books

parts.note: a learned person is wise
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A buffalo turns up in scholarly volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing in' is a link, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The wisent is the European species of wild ox, close cousin of the American buffalo.

clue.text: Expert in converting disagreeable conconction back into drink

indicators.note: one piece is placed into the other

parts.note: beer is a drink

indicators.note: the word for the unpleasant mixture is read backwards

parts.note: a mess is an unappetising concoction; the page misprints the second word

explanation.surface: A specialist in transforming a revolting brew back into something drinkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MESS into SSEM, which goes into BEER. Henry Bessemer devised the converter that turns pig iron into steel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Bessemer invented the steelmaking converter, so he was a master of that transforming process.

clue.text: Restaurant in which clubs wine and dine, entertained by song

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for the suit of clubs in card games

indicators.note: the song plays host, holding the other piece within it

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera
to fete someone is to entertain them lavishly

explanation.surface: An eatery where club members feast while being serenaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertained by' is a containment signal; 'wine and dine' reads as the restaurant's activity, but it is one verb meaning to treat lavishly.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service eating place where diners collect their own food from a counter.

clue.text: Mouthpiece giving source of heart attack?

definitions.meaning: the double curve of the upper lip, a feature of the mouth
the Roman love god's weapon, whose arrows strike hearts

explanation.surface: A medical question about what in the mouth sets off a cardiac arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart attack' is not medical: the love god's arrows strike hearts, launched from his weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the curved upper lip line, and literally the archer god of love's weapon that sends arrows at lovers.

clue.text: Following setback, energy is put into literary output

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: the energy letter is inserted within the word for setback

parts.note: a reverse is a setback or defeat
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: After a reversal of fortune, a writer puts effort into their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is put into' places E inside REVERSE, after F for following.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry without regular metre or rhyme is a form of written creative work.

clue.text: Engine of war the heartless butcher deployed

indicators.note: troops deployed are arranged into new positions, so the letters are rearranged
without its central letter, the middle of the three-letter word

explanation.surface: A cruel slaughterman puts a military machine to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' strips the H from 'the', leaving TE; 'deployed' rearranges TE plus BUTCHER.
explanation.definitionFit: The trebuchet was a medieval siege catapult using a counterweight to hurl stones at walls.

clue.text: Rising level of noise following extremely rude celebrity

indicators.note: the noise unit comes after the letters taken from rude
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the bel is a unit measuring sound intensity, ten decibels
a lion is a celebrated person, as in a literary lion

explanation.surface: Ever-louder noise follows a crude famous person around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely rude' gives RE, the first and last letters of 'rude'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is an uprising or revolt against authority, so the noun means revolt.

clue.text: A long letter

parts.note: to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: A lengthy piece of correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' is a verb, to yearn, not an adjective describing the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The written name of the eighth letter of the alphabet is spelt this way.

clue.text: Gunman?

parts.note: split into two: slang for a firearm, and a chess man on the board; both are one word

explanation.definitionFit: Slang calls a handgun this, and chessmen are pieces, so one word serves gun and man.

clue.text: Corolla's opening in flatter flower

indicators.note: the single letter is placed inside the phrase for flatter

parts.note: to butter up is to flatter

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The first petals open within a showy bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' picks the first letter and 'in' marks the insertion. A corolla is a flower's ring of petals, a fitting decoy beside the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttercup is a common yellow wild flower of the genus Ranunculus.

clue.text: Street light outside reveals barman

indicators.note: the word for a light goes outside the street abbreviation

parts.note: a taper is a thin candle used for lighting

explanation.surface: A lamp in the street shows a bartender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' marks the wrap; 'Street light' reads as a lamp post, but splits into two separate pieces, and 'reveals' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster is an old word for a person who draws and serves beer at a bar.

clue.text: Run into and split defence

parts.note: to ram is to crash into
to part is to split or separate

explanation.surface: An attacker charges at the defensive line and breaks through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run into' looks like it might mean R placed inside; it is RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is a defensive wall or bank surrounding a fort.

clue.text: Opuntia growing wild in ideal state

definitions.note: the definition is an adjectival phrase, matching the adjective answer

indicators.note: a plant growing wild spreads untamed, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A prickly pear cactus flourishes untamed in perfect conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: Opuntia is the prickly pear cactus, which looks like the subject; it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's Utopia was an imagined perfect commonwealth, so the adjective describes perfection.

clue.text: Wholeheartedly mixing love and duty

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are mixed together into a new order

explanation.surface: Combining affection and obligation with full commitment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixing' shuffles LOVE and DUTY together; 'and' is not fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something devoutly means doing it with earnest sincerity and complete commitment.

clue.text: Gun dogs

definitions.meaning: the name of a quick-firing automatic cannon, especially an anti-aircraft gun
two Pomeranian dogs, each called a pom

explanation.surface: Firearms and hounds, as on a shooting trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gun dogs' reads as retrievers; split it into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid-firing naval anti-aircraft cannon had this name, and two Pomeranians are each a pom.

clue.text: Heir's due to dock and put down, according to report

indicators.note: as reported by voice, so the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to berth is to dock a ship, and to write is to put down on paper

explanation.surface: An inheritance is to be moored and recorded, so the account says.
explanation.walkthrough: BERTH plus WRITE, said aloud, sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthright is what someone is entitled to by birth, such as an inheritance owed to an heir.

clue.text: A side's joined the alliance

parts.note: a side is a team of eleven, XI in Roman numerals, and the 's supplies S

explanation.surface: A team has signed up to the coalition.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the Axis, the alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Axis powers were the Second World War coalition led by Germany, Italy and Japan.

clue.text: Forcefully removing novice driver from sport

indicators.note: the learner letter is taken away from the sport

parts.note: wrestling is a sport
L is the learner plate on a British novice driver's car

explanation.surface: A learner motorist is wrenched out of a sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L plate, so L stands for a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: Wresting means seizing or extracting by force, as in wresting control.

clue.text: Circular barrel in American gun

indicators.note: the barrel word sits inside the gun word

parts.note: rod is American slang for a pistol
a tun is a large cask or barrel

explanation.surface: A round barrel, as in the muzzle of an American weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barrel' looks like a gun part; it is a cask, TUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotund means round in shape, a synonym for circular, also used of plump people.
